info.name: Eventrix Backend API
info.description:
Postman collection for the current Eventrix backend routes.

🔑 TOKEN FLOW:
1. Bootstrap an admin with POST /admins/bootstrap or create one with POST /admins after login.
2. Log in with POST /auth/login and store the returned token in {{accessToken}}.
3. All protected requests reuse {{accessToken}}.
4. POST /events auto-creates the organizer profile for the logged-in user and returns organizerId for follow-up organizer requests.
5. Runtime env keys used by the backend include DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_URL_POOLER, JWT_SECRET, JWT_EXPIRES_IN, FRONTEND_URL, GATEWAY_FEE_PERCENT, GATEWAY_FEE_FLAT, REFUND_WINDOW_HOURS, PAYOUT_DELAY_DAYS, SUPABASE_URL, and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.

📤 FILE UPLOADS: POST /uploads/signed-url with a purpose (profile-picture | event-image | event-cover | company-logo) to get a signed Supabase PUT URL, PUT the file bytes to it directly, then send the returned publicUrl as a normal string field on the participant/event/organizer create-or-update call. See multipart.md. Requires SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (note the _ROLE_ — not SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, an older/removed variable name) in your local .env, or this now returns a 503 with a clear message instead of a raw 500.

👤 ORGANIZER SELF-SERVICE: PATCH/DELETE /organizers/:id now accepts an organizer's own token (not just admin) to manage their own profile, gated by ownership in the handler; admin-only fields (commissionRate, commissionFlatFee, verificationLevel, autoApproveEvents) still 403 for non-admins. See the two 'Update Organizer' requests and the admin-only-field negative test below.

💳 PAYMENT STATUS ENFORCEMENT: POST /payments/refunds and POST /events/check-in now both require the enrollment's paymentStatus to be "paid" — not just status "confirmed". A paid-ticket enrollment starts out paymentStatus:"pending" until POST /payments/webhook confirms it (free tickets are marked paymentStatus:"paid" immediately at enroll time, no webhook needed). Calling Request Refund or Check In before the webhook now correctly 400s instead of silently succeeding against an unpaid booking. Also: a late/duplicate webhook can no longer resurrect an already-refunded or cancelled enrollment back to confirmed/paid — see the 'Request Refund' + 'Payment Webhook' sequence below.

🧪 RECOMMENDED RUN ORDER:
1. POST /auth/register for a regular user.
2. POST /admins/bootstrap to seed the first admin record.
3. POST /auth/login to capture {{accessToken}}.
4. POST /admins to create a protected admin record.
5. POST /categories then POST /categories/bulk to capture 3 distinct category IDs (categoryId, categoryId2, categoryId3) — PUT /users/me/interests requires 3 unique IDs, duplicates now 400.
6. POST /events to capture eventId and organizerId.
7. GET /events/my-events and GET /events/pending to verify event visibility.
8. POST /participants plus the users/me profile routes — Create Participant now returns an accessToken too (same as auth/register), since it creates the same kind of account.
9. POST /events/:id/enroll captures enrollmentId and ticketCode.
10. POST /events/check-in and POST /payments/refunds (Request Refund), each run once immediately after enroll on a paid ticket — expect 400 on both, payment isn't confirmed yet.
11. POST /payments/webhook confirms the payment (paymentStatus -> "paid").
12. Re-run POST /events/check-in — now succeeds. Re-run POST /payments/refunds — now succeeds and captures refundId.
13. Use the captured IDs for the remaining refund/approve/reject and delete flows.
